title: Shapes more than one spec schema names
description: Not a spec kind. `closure` spec §2.6 and `validator` spec §6.1 describe `body` as deliberately the same thing — 'a validator is a special kind of task, so what does this thing do and how do I run it should have one answer in the system, not two'. This file is that one answer, `$ref`-ed from both.

body.description: What this thing actually is: what the work is, what to execute, and how. `readme.md` is always required — a task nobody can read is a step nobody can review, and that holds for a non-leaf too. `entry.sh` is required iff the body is programmatic, and it is what makes it programmatic. Whether exactly one of `entry` and a subgraph is present is a named load-time check, not a schema keyword: `if`/`then` produces a message nobody can act on.

readme.description: Package-relative path to the readme.md. For an agent task this IS the body — the description the agent works from.

entry.description: Package-relative path to the entry.sh: the exact execution entry point. May run something on the system or run material a handoff supplied.

materials.description: Package-relative paths this body needs for itself. How these become a handoff is undecided — docs/interfaces.md §5.1b — so nothing reads them yet.

name.description: Unique within this spec kind's registry. This is the vocabulary entry every reference to this spec is drawn from, so it is an identifier rather than free text.

version.description: This spec's own revision. **Maintenance metadata only** — nothing at runtime reads it, nothing pins to it, and loading two versions of one spec at once is not supported (closure spec §1.2).

description.description: What this is, for a human.

handoff_kind_names.description: Handoff KIND names, never ids. A grant or a declaration is written where no instance exists. **Deliberately not `uniqueItems`**: `handoff` criterion 11 requires that a task with two inputs of the same kind is unambiguous, so a repeated kind is a supported case rather than a typo.
